previous_description: Defines validation rules for JSON array instances, constraining item schemas, cardinality bounds (minItems/maxItems), uniqueness requirements, and contains-subschema matching.
definition: A JSON Schema subschema with type 'array' that constrains an ordered list of values: the schema each element must satisfy, how many elements are allowed, whether they must be distinct, and whether at least one element must match a given subschema.

distinguish_from.when: you are modelling the named field that holds the list (its name, title, description, readOnly) rather than the constraints on the list value itself.
the collection is keyed by name rather than ordered by position, such as a Map<String, T>, dict or record type, which becomes an object with additionalProperties or patternProperties.
the list type is declared once under 'definitions' with a title and reused through $ref. Model the array constraints inside it as an arrayschema.
the constraint is a boolean combination (allOf/anyOf/oneOf/not) of subschemas, for example a union of element types, rather than array keywords directly.

standard_reference: JSON Schema Draft 7 Validation (draft-handrews-json-schema-validation-01) §6.4 Validation Keywords for Arrays (items, additionalItems, maxItems, minItems, uniqueItems, contains)
code_evidence: A DTO, entity or record field typed as a collection, such as List<T>, T[], Array<T>, Set<T>, Sequence[T] or repeated in protobuf, where Set or frozenset types imply uniqueItems.

Cardinality validators on a collection field, such as Bean Validation @Size(min, max) or @NotEmpty on a List, Pydantic conlist or Field(min_length=..., max_length=...), or Zod z.array(...).min().max().nonempty().
A JSON Schema or OpenAPI fragment containing "type": "array" together with an "items" keyword, often with minItems, maxItems or uniqueItems.

attribute_descriptions.name: type
attribute_descriptions.description: The JSON Schema type keyword, which for this element must be the literal string 'array'. Always set it so the schema validates only array instances.

attribute_descriptions.name: items
attribute_descriptions.description: The subschema, inline or as a $ref to a definition, that every array element must validate against. Set it whenever the element type is known, for example the T in List<T>.

attribute_descriptions.name: minItems
attribute_descriptions.description: A non-negative integer giving the inclusive minimum number of elements. Set it when the list must not be empty (1) or needs a floor, for example from @Size(min) or @NotEmpty.

attribute_descriptions.name: maxItems
attribute_descriptions.description: A non-negative integer giving the inclusive maximum number of elements. Set it when code or configuration enforces an upper bound on list length, for example @Size(max) or a page-size limit.

attribute_descriptions.name: uniqueItems
attribute_descriptions.description: When true, all elements must be pairwise distinct by JSON equality. Set it when the source type has set semantics or the code rejects duplicates.

attribute_descriptions.name: contains
attribute_descriptions.description: A subschema (inline or $ref) that at least one element must validate against. Set it only when the code requires the list to include a matching element, such as at least one primary address.

notes: 'type' is typed 'any' and optional. It should be a required string fixed to 'array'. 'items' as a string cannot express Draft 7's tuple form (an array of schemas). 'additionalItems' is missing. The aggregates relationships omit arrayschema→arrayschema (nested arrays) and boolean element types.
